spillover_issues.body:
🤖 Drafted with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

## TL;DR

A single launch should be able to absorb TPU capacity wherever it's available across regions, with `--prefix mirror://` handling dedup. iris natively supports this via `region IN [a, b, c]` constraints, but marin's executor pre-collapses each TPU step's allowed regions to a single one before fray builds the JobRequest, so iris's per-job multi-region matching never runs. Two design options below (one targeted patch, one structural simplification). Maintainer input on which direction to pursue would unblock a PR.

## Motivation

The goal is to run executor steps in whichever region has available TPU capacity and dedup completed work across regions via `mirror://`. iris already supports per-job multi-region matching (`region_constraint` with `op=IN`, `iris/cluster/constraints.py:329`) — its scheduler picks across listed regions by capacity. Marin's executor is what prevents that from working.

## What the executor does today

`_resolve_steps` runs three things per TPU step before submission:

1. **`_step_dag_tpu_regions`** (`executor.py:424`) queries the iris autoscaler via `_regions_for_tpu_variants_from_iris` (`:356`) for which regions have the requested variant. The recursive `regions_for_step` also propagates upward: a CPU step inherits the region set of any TPU dependents. So a CPU prompts step that has TPU completion-cell dependents ends up with a non-`None` `dag_tpu_regions`.

2. **`_component_tpu_pins`** (`:468`) builds adjacency over `relevant_steps` (steps with `dag_tpu_regions != None`), walks connected components, and for each one picks `chosen_region = sorted(component_regions)[0]` (`:531`). Every step in the component gets pinned to that single region.

3. **`_maybe_attach_inferred_region_constraint`** (`:547`) receives `forced_region=chosen_region` and rewrites `step.fn.resources.regions = [chosen_region]`.

Fray then turns that into `region IN [chosen_region]` — a one-element constraint — on the JobRequest. The iris client (`iris/client/client.py:643`) sees a region constraint exists and skips its auto-inherit branch. iris's scheduler is left with a single-region constraint and can only place there.

## Worst case: eval sweeps

`make_eval_step` (`experiments/downstream_scaling/evals/framework/core.py`) produces `prompts (CPU) → completions (TPU) → grade (CPU)` per cell, with the **prompts step shared** across all cells with the same task config (executor dedups by hash). Upward propagation in `_step_dag_tpu_regions` means the shared prompts step ends up with a non-`None` `dag_tpu_regions`, gets pulled into `relevant_steps`, and forms an adjacency edge to every completion cell. The result: `prompts ∪ {all completion cells}` is one giant connected component, and the entire sweep collapses to `sorted(component_regions)[0]` — a single region — even though every cell is independent and there's no genuine gang-scheduling requirement.

## Why iris-level mechanisms can't substitute

`CoschedulingConfig(group_by=...)` (`iris/cluster/types.py:380`) ensures tasks **within a single iris job** share a worker attribute value (e.g., `tpu-name` for multi-host TPU pods). It's per-job, not cross-job. Marin submits each executor step as its own iris job, so iris coscheduling can't coordinate region placement across multiple steps. For genuine multi-step TPU pipelines that need gang scheduling, marin is the only layer that can enforce same-region placement.

## Existing workarounds and why none are sufficient

- **`iris job run --region a --region b ...`**: iris picks one region for the orchestrator; everything inherits it. Achieves "any region at launch" but not "any TPU per job."
- **Multiple staggered launches** sharing work via `mirror://`: works but adds operational complexity, and the per-step lock is per-bucket under `mirror://` (writes go to `gs://marin-{local}/.../.executor_status.lock`), so concurrent orchestrators in different regions can both succeed on `try_acquire_lock` for the same unclaimed cell. The `should_run` polling loop (`executor_step_status.py:186`) handles the case where the lock is *already visible* to another orchestrator via mirror scan, but doesn't close the acquisition-time race.
- **Restructure algorithms into CPU-executor-step + nested-fray-TPU shape** (what `iid_zephyr.py` and `rerank.py` already do): bypasses the executor's pinning because the outer step is CPU. Works, but requires rewriting `joint_decode.py` / `joint_decode_avg.py` (and any future TPU-on-executor-step algorithm) — not general.

None of these match "single launch, jobs go to any region with capacity" cleanly.

## Proposed fix — two options

Both are contained to `lib/marin/src/marin/execution/executor.py`. Run scripts and algorithms stay as they are; `worker_resources=ResourceConfig.with_tpu(tpu_types)` with `regions` unset is sufficient.

### Option A — targeted patch

Two coordinated edits.

**(a)** In `_step_dag_tpu_regions`'s `regions_for_step`, return `None` immediately when the step is CPU instead of iterating dependents:

```python
if step_regions is None:
    reachable_tpu_regions[step] = None
    return None
```

inserted between the `step_regions = _tpu_regions_for_remote_callable(...)` assignment and the existing `downstream_tpu_regions = step_regions` line.

**(b)** In `_component_tpu_pins`, short-circuit single-step components:

```python
if len(component) == 1:
    continue
```

inserted between the component-building `while stack:` loop and the `component_regions: set[str] | None = None` initialization.

Effect: standalone TPU steps fall through `_maybe_attach_inferred_region_constraint`'s `regions = sorted(allowed_regions)` branch, fray attaches `region IN [...]`, iris auto-inherit skips because a constraint is present, iris's scheduler picks per-job by capacity. Multi-step TPU-direct components (TPU↔TPU edges, after edit (a) removes CPU intermediaries) still get pinned the way they do today.

### Option B — region-agnostic executor

Delete `_step_dag_tpu_regions`, `_component_tpu_pins`, and the forced-region path in `_maybe_attach_inferred_region_constraint`. The executor stops inferring or rewriting regions. Scripts set `regions=` explicitly on TPU resources:

```python
ALLOWED_REGIONS = ["us-east5", "europe-west4", "us-central1"]
worker_resources=ResourceConfig.with_tpu(tpu_types, regions=ALLOWED_REGIONS)
```

iris auto-inherit doesn't override an existing constraint; iris's scheduler picks per-job. CPU steps without `regions` set inherit parent's region naturally. Multi-step TPU gang scheduling becomes script-author responsibility (set the same single region across the relevant steps).

## Tradeoff

- **Option A** preserves the framework's auto-inference for TPU steps and keeps run scripts plumbing-free, at the cost of keeping the TPU/CPU distinction inside the executor.
- **Option B** is structurally simpler — executor knows nothing about regions — but pushes the explicit region list into every TPU-using run script and makes gang scheduling a script-level concern.

## Open questions for maintainers

- Are there pipelines in `experiments/` that rely on TPU-CPU-TPU chains for cross-step gang scheduling? After option A (a), the CPU intermediary no longer bridges upstream and downstream TPU steps in the component graph, so they'd land in separate components and could go to different regions. If this case exists and matters, option A needs a different formulation; option B makes the requirement explicit at the script level.
- Should the multi-region list come from the iris autoscaler's *configured* groups (current behavior of `_regions_for_tpu_variant_from_iris`) or from a more conservative source (live capacity, allow-list)?
- Anything specific the fallthrough's `sorted(allowed_regions)` ordering should preserve for iris?

## Acceptance criteria

A single `executor_main` launch with `--prefix mirror://` and `worker_resources=ResourceConfig.with_tpu(tpu_types)` (no `regions=` set in script) results in:

- Each TPU step's JobRequest carries `region IN [autoscaler-configured regions]` rather than `region IN [single]`.
- iris's scheduler distributes the cells across regions according to live capacity.
- `mirror://` dedups completed cells across regions correctly.
- No regression for multi-step TPU pipelines that genuinely need gang scheduling (single-region pinning still happens for size > 1 TPU components under option A).

spillover_issues.body:
🤖 Agent-generated issue (summary of an autonomous experiment run).

## Goal
Port the PyTorch `HybridMuon` optimizer (`opt_a` / `opt_f` variants, from github.com/mahyarjn80/Opt_Smuon) to JAX/Levanter and reproduce the PRISM-Berkeley Qwen3 scaling LR-sweep setting (#4933) with it, to compare the two variants. Code in PR #6118. W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/speedrun (runs `qwen3_{size}_hybrid_muon_{a,f}_4096_lrx*`).

## Optimizer
HybridMuon = Muon Newton–Schulz orthogonalization of the (Nesterov) momentum, blended with a nuclear-norm/effective-rank rescaling (two closed-form blends, "a" and "f"). Nuclear norm via the polar-factor identity `⟨orth,g⟩=‖g‖_*`. Linear weights → hybrid transform; embeddings/lm_head/bias → AdamW. Details in PR #6118.

## Setup (reproducing #4933, trimmed)
- Sizes 130m / 300m / 520m (llama presets → Qwen3, seq 4096), fineweb-edu-10B, linear schedule, per-size centers/batch/steps from #4933.
- LR sweep: {0.5, 0.75, 1.0} × per-size center, both variants. (Trimmed from the original {0.5…1.5}×4-size grid — see "Infra" below.)
- Region-pinned single-region (no cross-region I/O), logged to marin-community/speedrun.

## Results

Final `train/loss` (lower = better):

| size | LR× | **opt_a** | **opt_f** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 130m | 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0 | 3.390 / **3.328** / 3.417 | 3.842 / 3.896 / 3.895 |
| 300m | 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0 | 3.054 / 3.040 / **3.022** | — / 3.149 / — |

**Findings**
1. **`opt_a` clearly outperforms `opt_f`** at every (size, LR): ~0.5 lower loss at 130m, ~0.13 lower at 300m (lrx0_75). `opt_a` has a clear LR optimum (~lrx0_75); `opt_f` is ~flat across LR.
2. **`opt_f` converges — no divergence**, despite ~8× larger raw update norms than `opt_a` at the same LR. It's simply a weaker optimizer here.
3. `opt_a` size-scaling: 130m best 3.328 → 300m best 3.022 (as expected).
4. 520m and the remaining `opt_f` LR points were still training when stopped, but the `opt_a > opt_f` verdict is already conclusive from 130m + 300m.

## Status
**Stopped.** Most of the sweep (130m + 300m fully; 520m partial) completed on preemptible v5p; the tail was grinding slowly under capacity contention and was wound down since the result was conclusive.

## Infra notes (debugging lessons; cost me real time, worth recording)
- **`--extra tpu` is required** for iris TPU launches. Without it the worker `uv sync`s the default jax-0.10 line with **no libtpu** → `libtpu.so: cannot open shared object file` → JAX falls back to CPU → `RuntimeError: No accelerator found`, which iris mislabels as a "bad node" and auto-retries forever. Read logs for `libtpu.so` before blaming hardware.
- **Coordinator/region co-location:** pinning only the child steps' `regions=[...]` isn't enough — the executor coordinator does constant `.executor_status.lock` bookkeeping on `MARIN_PREFIX`; if it runs in a different region, every lock op is cross-region egress (amplified by retries). Pin the coordinator too (`iris job run --region …`, which is mutually exclusive with `--reserve`).
- **Preemptible coordinator churn:** the preemptible CPU coordinator got preempted every ~15–30 min; each restart tore down children and reset progress. We trimmed scope (dropped 1_2b + high LRs) to make completion feasible and kept relaunching on stall.

| **Muon** | 1.1663 | 1.0582 |

| MuonRemez | 1.1761 | 1.0654 |

### Verdict
**Plain Muon beats HybridMuon variant `a`** on C4-EN BPB at both sizes (~0.017 at 130m, ~0.028 at 300m). ## Summary

This experiment added correctness-first GrugMoE inference support across the Marin, vLLM, and tpu-inference handoff branches. The work mapped GrugMoE/Levanter semantics into vLLM with an unfused PyTorch `GrugMoeForCausalLM`, added tpu-inference auto-routing for that model type, and created a Marin parity harness that compares tiny seeded GrugMoE components and full hidden states against the Levanter/JAX reference. Local component and composed parity checks passed, then Iris validated the same strict-parity harness on a `v6e-4` TPU in `europe-west4` after resolving setup issues around SSH keys, TPU runtime extras, and TPU matmul precision. The current conclusion is that initial correctness support is validated; performance work, checkpoint export/loading, and real-model end-to-end smoke tests remain out of scope for this issue.

### Helpful links
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/grugmoe-vllm-tpu-support
- https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/tree/grugmoe-vllm-tpu-support
- https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/tree/grugmoe-vllm-tpu-support
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6106#issuecomment-4598509275

## Objective

Add initial correctness-first GrugMoE inference support to vLLM TPU, with Levanter as the correctness reference and tiny seeded random GrugMoE configs. Performance, Levanter checkpoint export, vLLM checkpoint loading, and real-model end-to-end smoke tests are out of scope.

## Gates

1. Repo map: identify GrugMoE in Marin/Levanter, vLLM/tpu-inference extension points, closest reusable model implementations, and the smallest useful dummy config.
2. Component parity: port/test GrugMoE components in isolation against Levanter with tiny seeded tensors.
3. Composed parity: assemble the minimal full GrugMoE forward path and compare against Levanter on the tiny random model.
4. TPU validation: run targeted correctness tests on one Dev TPU `v6e-4` slice in `europe-west4` via Iris, interactive priority.
5. Handoff: leave branch(es), tests/harnesses, issue notes, logbook/reference markdown, exact commands, blockers, and next steps.

1. **Trigger.** What counts as \"end of a job\" — last N% of shards remaining, or queue empty while shards still in-flight? What counts as \"idle capacity\" — workers polling \`pull_task\` with an empty queue?
2. **Straggler detection.** Heartbeat-based progress (per-row counters), wallclock vs. median completed-shard time, or per-stage threshold? Min sample size before flagging?

5. **Definition of done.** Acceptance metric — e.g., end-to-end wallclock reduction on a synthetic skewed workload, or a specific production pipeline?

Without (3) especially, a speculative-execution PR risks corrupting shard outputs. Happy to pick this up once the design is nailed down, or to draft a design doc per \`.agents/skills/write-design-doc/\` if that's preferred.

spillover_issues.body:
## Description

The `marin.inference.distributed` API on `XenonMolecule/marin@inference/distributed-library` cannot be used by vendoring only `lib/marin/src/marin/inference/distributed/` into a worktree on `main`.

All 14 named cross-package imports resolve cleanly against current `main`, so the integration looks viable at static-check time. At runtime, `regional_job._build_context` (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/distributed/regional_job.py:118-140`) passes `worker_environment=...` to `ZephyrContext`, but main's `ZephyrContext.__init__` doesn't accept it:

```
TypeError: ZephyrContext.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'worker_environment'
```

That kwarg is the library's only path for setting JAX/vLLM XLA cache env vars on workers (`compile_cache.py:65-79`), so without it the compile cache — the library's headline feature — is unusable. The whole-branch `pip install` works because the supporting `lib/zephyr/` change ships on the same branch; vendoring just the `distributed/` subtree silently drops it.

Repro: vendor `lib/marin/src/marin/inference/distributed/` into a worktree on `main`, write a script that calls `marin.inference.distributed.inference(model, dataset, config)` from an iris coordinator with `compile_cache_uri_template` set. Regional jobs crash with the TypeError in their entrypoint before any TPU worker spawns.

### Definition of Done

Either (a) document on the fork branch (e.g., in `DESIGN.md`) the full set of supporting PRs that must land before the API is usable from main — at minimum the `ZephyrContext.worker_environment` change in `lib/zephyr/`, plus any related `lib/fray/` / `lib/rigging/` changes — or (b) land those supporting PRs into main and confirm `inference()` runs end-to-end from a worktree on main without local patches to `lib/zephyr/`.

comments.author: ahmeda14960
comments.body:
🤖 Update from running this end-to-end: **the cascade is 3 layers, not 2**.

After cherry-picking the `worker_environment` kwarg onto `ZephyrContext` (`lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py`, ~10 lines additive, sufficient to get past `regional_job._build_context`), the next layer down crashes with:

```
TypeError: ZephyrWorker.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'environment'
```

…inside the Zephyr worker actor. The fork branch also modifies `lib/fray/` to wire `environment=` through the fray actor system so it lands as worker process env rather than being forwarded to `ZephyrWorker.__init__`. The diff stat on `XenonMolecule/marin@inference/distributed-library` vs current `main` for `lib/fray/`:

```
 lib/fray/src/fray/client.py        | 10 ++++++++--
 lib/fray/src/fray/iris_backend.py  | 11 ++++++++++-
 lib/fray/src/fray/local_backend.py |  9 ++++++++-
```

So adopting the library from `main` requires three coordinated change-sets, not one:

1. Vendor `lib/marin/src/marin/inference/distributed/` (12 files) — already pulled.
2. Patch `lib/zephyr/src/zephyr/execution.py` — adds `worker_environment` kwarg to `ZephyrContext` and threads it through `_CoordinatorJobConfig` to `worker_group.create(environment=...)`.
3. Patch `lib/fray/{client,iris_backend,local_backend}.py` — wires `environment=` through fray's actor-creation path so workers receive it as env vars rather than constructor kwargs.

Repro confirmed at 1e21 (3.4B) and 1e22 (9.7B): coordinator init succeeds (post layer-1 patch), worker construction loops on the `ZephyrWorker.__init__()` TypeError until retries exhaust.

Updating the Definition of Done to reflect this: the supporting PRs that must land in `main` are at minimum the lib/zephyr/ + lib/fray/ deltas above, not just zephyr.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Description
Add a FEVER-based factuality probe for the perplexity-gap suite. The slice should measure evidence-conditioned factual discrimination and abstention, not open-ended generation. Use train/dev data only, avoid test questions, and stage records in a neutral few-shot supervised target-only format:

```text
evidence:
...
claim:
...
verdict:
```

Targets should be `supports`, `refutes`, or `not enough information`. Balance few-shot examples across labels. For `NOT ENOUGH INFORMATION`, avoid making the metric only “empty evidence means NEI”; prefer retrieved or distractor evidence when practical, or split claim-only NEI into a clearly named diagnostic subset.

### Definition of Done
- Register a pinned FEVER source with eval-only policy and provenance.
- Stage at least one supervised target-only FEVER validation slice with balanced labels and neutral few-shot prompts.
- Add focused tests for rendering, label mapping, and target-only dataset registration.
- Include the new slice in the 32B perplexity-gap workflow without using FEVER test data.

comments.body:

- [x] Read AGENTS.md, fix-issue/SKILL.md, pull-request/SKILL.md

# Research

The perplexity-gap suite renders raw text PPL through bundles registered in [`perplexity_gap_registry.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py). `RawTextEvaluationDataset` already supports a target-only supervised path via [`supervised_text_dataset`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/perplexity_gap.py#L113-L138) (input_key/target_key → `SupervisedLmDatasetFormat`). The 32B leg of the matrix is just `marin_32b` + `qwen3_32b` rows in the registry — adding a new bundle automatically expands across them. The closest precedent for ingestion-manifest + staged supervised slices is [`structured_evals.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/structured_evals.py) (#5129, ~1800 LOC across 7 files).

**Relevant code**
- [`perplexity_gap_registry.py#L72-L110`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/perplexity_gap_registry.py#L72-L110) — bundle registration
- [`perplexity_gap.py#L113-L138`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/perplexity_gap.py#L113-L138) — `supervised_text_dataset` helper
- [`structured_evals.py#L74-L236`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/structured_evals.py#L74-L236) — `IngestionSourceManifest` + eval-only policy template
- [`ingestion_manifest.py#L55-L83`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/ingestion_manifest.py#L55-L83) — `IngestionPolicy` shape (EVAL_ONLY, provenance)
- [`long_tail_ppl.py#L41-L65`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/long_tail_ppl.py#L41-L65) — slice/family dataclass + tagging convention

# Proposed Approach

Scope is comparable to #5129 (new staging transform + tests + registry wiring + experiment file), so I am pausing for review before implementation.

Pinned source. FEVER v1.0 (`fever/fever`, config `v1.0`) at a pinned HF revision. Use `labelled_dev` for the staged validation slice. Explicitly avoid `paper_test` / `paper_dev`. Eval-only policy with provenance noting Wikipedia-derived claims and contamination risk.

Staging transform. New `lib/marin/src/marin/transform/structured_text/fever_factuality.py` that reads pinned parquet, normalizes labels (`SUPPORTS` → `supports`, `REFUTES` → `refutes`, `NOT ENOUGH INFO` → `not enough information`), joins evidence sentences (from the FEVER evidence annotations) into the `evidence:\n...\nclaim:\n...\nverdict:` prompt body, and emits `{input, target}` records. The target is the verdict string only; the prompt prefix lives in `input`. Few-shot examples are sampled from train, balanced 1:1:1 across labels with a fixed seed, and prepended into `input` per example. Hash inputs through `IngestionSourceManifest.fingerprint()` like the existing staged sources do.

NEI handling. Per the issue: do not let "empty evidence" be the only NEI signal. Split NEI into two named diagnostic sub-slices:
- `fever_nei_retrieved` — NEI claims paired with distractor evidence sampled from the same Wikipedia page (or a near-neighbor page).
- `fever_nei_claim_only` — NEI claims with empty evidence, kept as a separate diagnostic so it does not dominate the headline metric.

`supports` / `refutes` keep their gold evidence sentences.

Registry wiring. Add `fever_factuality_bundle()` to `perplexity_gap_registry.py` returning a `PerplexityGapBundle` with the three slices (`supports`, `refutes`, balanced + the two NEI variants — final keying: `fever/v1.0/labelled_dev_balanced`, `fever/v1.0/labelled_dev_nei_retrieved`, `fever/v1.0/labelled_dev_nei_claim_only`). Append to `registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()` so it expands across all models including `marin_32b` / `qwen3_32b` automatically. No new experiment file needed — the existing `exp_model_perplexity_gap_coverage_matrix.py` picks it up.

Tests. New `tests/evals/test_fever_factuality.py`:
- Label-mapping round trip on a tiny fixture (3 records, one per label) — verifies `SUPPORTS`/`REFUTES`/`NOT ENOUGH INFO` → lowercase target strings and rejects unknown labels.
- Prompt rendering on a single record — verifies exact `evidence:\n{...}\nclaim:\n{...}\nverdict:` layout and that the target is `verdict` text only (no trailing newline).
- Balanced few-shot sampler — verifies equal label counts per shot block, deterministic under fixed seed.
- NEI diagnostic split — verifies `fever_nei_claim_only` has empty evidence and `fever_nei_retrieved` does not.
- Registration — `fever_factuality_bundle()` appears in `registered_perplexity_gap_bundles()` and is keyed under the bundle name in the coverage plan for both `marin_32b` and `qwen3_32b`.

Estimated size: ~600-900 LOC across 4 files (staging transform, experiment registration, tests, manifest entry). Asking for review on (a) NEI split strategy, (b) few-shot count (proposing 4 balanced shots = 12 examples in context), (c) whether to add a `fever_factuality.py` experiment file separate from `perplexity_gap_registry.py`.

spillover_issues.body:
Grug MoE stores scanned transformer blocks in [`haliax.nn.ArrayStacked`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dcd89eeb1de15fef194ac9dfd125eb5269882dde/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1189-L1203). Parameter and gradient watch metrics consequently collapse the leading layer axis into one norm per stacked parameter. The W&B metric keys contain no layer index, so a layer with abnormal parameter or gradient growth cannot be identified.

Reproduce:
1. Run a Grug MoE configuration with norm watching enabled and `WatchConfig.split_scan_layers=True`.
2. Inspect the `params/norm/*stacked_blocks*` and `grad/norm/*stacked_blocks*` metrics in W&B.
3. Observe one metric per stacked parameter, reduced across every layer, instead of one metric per layer.

Expected: `split_scan_layers=True` emits separate parameter and gradient norms for every `ArrayStacked` layer, with stable layer indices in the metric keys.

[`summary_statistics_for_tree`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dcd89eeb1de15fef194ac9dfd125eb5269882dde/lib/levanter/src/levanter/analysis/tree_stats.py#L45-L77) only recognizes `haliax.nn.Stacked` as a split scan container. The [Grug watch path](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dcd89eeb1de15fef194ac9dfd125eb5269882dde/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/train.py#L744-L756) forwards `split_scan_layers`, but its `ArrayStacked` model cannot use that branch.

spillover_issues.author: wmoss
spillover_issues.body:
Iris controller restarts today are driven entirely by `iris cluster controller restart` (see `lib/iris/OPS.md`, `.agents/skills/restart-iris/`) — GCE clusters restart via SSH + `docker restart`, CoreWeave clusters via the Kubernetes API — not by Pulumi. This is an investigation, not a commitment to migrate: the restart flow has safety properties that a naive Pulumi resource-replace would break if not carried over deliberately.

Specifically: the controller keeps local SQLite state plus periodic GCS checkpoints, and restart takes a pre-restart checkpoint and writes a rollout record (image + matching checkpoint ref) so a failed health check can roll back atomically. DB migrations are forward-only and some are destructive, so restoring an old controller image without its paired pre-migration checkpoint breaks. Any Pulumi-driven approach needs to preserve this checkpoint-before-restart / paired-rollback behavior, e.g. by keeping restart-with-rollback as a wrapped CLI step (similar to how `iac.iris.service` wraps a CLI today) rather than modeling the controller as a plain replaceable resource.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Investigation, not a bug fix — no PR. Analysis below; handing off to a human for the migrate/don't-migrate call.

# Research

Confirmed the issue body against the code. `iris cluster controller restart` is a CLI-side choreography around a mechanical platform restart; the safety lives in the CLI, not in the platform primitive.

Forward deploy in [`cli/cluster.py:controller_restart` L1117-1215](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1117-L1215): pre-deploy checkpoint (L1180) → build fresh images (L1182) → write `PENDING` rollout record (L1187) → `restart_controller` (L1199) → on health-check failure `_auto_rollback` to previous image + its pre-deploy checkpoint (L1202) → write `COMMITTED` (L1206). `--rollback` (L1148) reverts to the recorded previous image + checkpoint.

The rollout record is a small state machine in GCS remote state, not in any deploy tool's state; the restarted controller consumes `ROLLBACK_REQUESTED` once on boot and self-clears. Migrations are forward-only and some are destructive, so an old image must boot on its paired pre-migration checkpoint — this is why image and checkpoint are recorded as a pair.

**Relevant code**
- [`cli/cluster.py#L1117`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1117) - restart/rollback choreography (checkpoint, record, restart, auto-rollback)
- [`controller/rollout.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/rollout.py) - `RolloutPhase`/`RolloutRecord`, read/write in GCS remote state
- [`platforms/vm_lifecycle.py#L409`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/vm_lifecycle.py#L409) / [`k8s/controller.py#L517`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/controller.py#L517) - mechanical restart primitives (no safety logic)
- [`controller/migrations/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/migrations) - forward-only, sometimes destructive
- [`iac/iris/service.py#L156-L164`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/iris/service.py#L156-L164) - existing CLI-wrap template to reuse

# Proposed approach

Do **not** model the controller as a plain replaceable Pulumi resource. A resource-replace would tear down and recreate around the restart, bypassing the checkpoint/rollout-record choreography and losing atomic rollback on a bad deploy.

Instead reuse the pattern already in [`iac/iris/service.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/src/iac/iris/service.py) (and the sibling finelog migration in #7571): wrap `iris cluster controller restart` in a `command.local.Command` component whose `create`/`update` verb runs the restart CLI and whose `delete` is a no-op (or `stop`, deliberately). Key the resource on the controller image tag plus a code hash so a change triggers `update` = restart-with-rollback; a failed health check propagates as a Command error, and the CLI has already auto-rolled-back. The rollout record stays in GCS remote state so `--rollback` keeps working out-of-band from Pulumi state.

Open questions for the human owner:
- Is the goal declarative *drift correction* (Pulumi restarts when image drifts) or just *inventory* (record the controller in the stack without owning restarts)? The wrapper above gives the former; only the latter avoids Pulumi ever triggering a restart.
- How should a Pulumi `up` that fails its health check and auto-rolls-back report to the operator — hard resource failure, or success-with-warning after rollback?
- Interaction with the manual `restart-iris` skill / direct CLI runs: Pulumi must treat an out-of-band restart as convergent, not as drift to undo.

Scope is a new Pulumi component plus wiring — multi-file design work, so leaving implementation to a human per the migration effort in #7571/#7262.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Investigation result: move Iris controller operations under the shared deploy interface, with Pulumi invoking the existing migration-aware restart transaction. Do not make the controller VM or Kubernetes Deployment a plain replaceable Pulumi resource.

Effort: medium, 2026-08-24. I stopped after the current code, linked PRs, Echo history, and Pulumi documentation converged on the same boundary.

### Current Marin context

The new work changes the operator interface, but not Iris's state-safety requirement:

- [#8537](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8537) provides one command tree for Pulumi applications. The executable merged there is `marin-deploy`, so the exact spelling today is `uv run marin-deploy ...`; adding a `deploy` script alias is independent of this design.
- [`controller restart`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1263-L1532) resolves secrets, checkpoints the live controller, builds and pins images, writes `PENDING`, restarts in place, health-checks, and commits or restores the previous image plus checkpoint. The controller [consumes the rollback request once](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/main.py#L51-L85).
- Pulumi [does not automatically roll back a failed update](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/support/faq/infrastructure/#automatic-rollbacks). Finelog therefore captures the active revision outside Pulumi, runs `pulumi up`, restores on failure, and refreshes state ([#7690](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7690), [current implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1936313ac7da5e1c4f08c0a1634e24cf66f4e772/lib/finelog/src/finelog/deploy/_k8s.py#L390-L471)). Iris needs that recovery boundary and its additional checkpoint pairing.

### Recommended first migration

1. Add a separate `infra/iris` application project with one stack per controller cluster. This follows the repository rule that application deploy lifecycles stay outside the static `infra/pulumi` substrate project.
2. Add an Iris controller component backed by `command.local.Command`. Its `create` and `update` verbs run the existing `iris cluster controller restart`; removal has no stop/delete verb. Inputs include the cluster, reviewed config hash, working-tree hash, and an explicit deploy generation for a forced same-tree restart. Pulumi's command provider runs `update` when inputs/triggers change instead of replacing the resource ([provider contract](https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/command/api-docs/local/command/)).
3. Add service-specific commands:

   ```text
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollout <cluster>
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollout <cluster> --force
   uv run marin-deploy iris rollback <cluster>
   ```

   `rollback` must call the existing `--rollback` path and use the GCS rollout record. Pulumi history is not a substitute for the recorded image/checkpoint pair. The rollout record remains the recovery source of truth; Pulumi records which reviewed tree/config triggered the transaction.
4. Keep the existing fleet gates: clean/current tree preflight, one cluster at a time, baseline snapshot, five-minute verification, and smoke job. Do not add Iris to the parallel path-triggered deployment matrix in the first change. That matrix cannot currently stop the fleet at the first failed cluster, and GCE restarts also require per-user SSH access.

This stage gives Iris the shared `marin-deploy` UX and Pulumi update/audit surface while preserving the current transaction even when an operator runs `pulumi up` directly.

### Native-resource follow-up

A later CoreWeave-only stage can adopt the non-secret runtime objects into an application stack: ConfigMap, protected PVC, Recreate Deployment, Service, PDB, node-agent DaemonSet, LocalQueue, and priority classes. It should proceed only after the deploy driver is split into prepare/activate/finalize/rollback operations and these conditions are tested:

- no workload mutation before a fresh checkpoint and `PENDING` record;
- every activation or health failure restores the recorded image and checkpoint, waits for `ROLLED_BACK`, then refreshes Pulumi state;
- direct `pulumi up` cannot bypass preparation;
- secret values remain outside Pulumi state;
- controller storage is protected, and GCE application changes never replace the controller VM;
- manual break-glass rollback remains convergent with the next intentional rollout.

Confidence is high for the first migration. Native CoreWeave ownership is feasible with those gates, but it is a separate lifecycle refactor; GCE should continue using the in-place SSH restart mechanism behind the same command.

### Handoff

No PR was opened because this request was an investigation. The next decision is whether to implement the first migration as scoped above and track native CoreWeave resource ownership separately.

🤖 ### Research

The shared deploy package currently dispatches Pulumi application projects, while Iris controller rollout still owns checkpoint, image build, activation, health, and paired rollback in [`controller_restart`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1263). GCE activation is duplicated across [Iris](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/gcp/handles.py#L176), [Finelog](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/src/finelog/deploy/_gcp.py#L205), and [Loom](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/loom/activate.sh). No open PR overlaps this migration.

### Proposed Fix

Add a generic GCE VM activation API to `marin-deploy`, plus an `infra/iris` application project and `deploy iris rollout|rollback` commands. The deploy wrapper will retain the current checkpoint and rollout-record transaction, pass a non-secret activation specification through Pulumi, and apply the paired previous image/checkpoint through the same Pulumi path when activation fails.

🤖 Implemented in [#8652](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8652).

Controller rollout and rollback now run through `uv run deploy iris rollout|rollback` and one restart-only Pulumi activation resource per cluster. A forward rollout takes a checkpoint and records the previous image/checkpoint pair before platform mutation. A failed candidate activates that pair through the same stack; a Pulumi failure before mutation restores the prior rollout record.

The GCE path uses a reusable `marin-deploy` startup-script activator with explicit SSH identity, retry, and metadata-persistence timing. CoreWeave continues to reconcile through Iris's Kubernetes provider. Pulumi deletion is a no-op, and resolved secrets and machine-local activation markers stay outside state. The old `iris cluster controller restart` command is removed, and the operator docs and fleet gates use the shared deploy command.

Validation passed: 20 `marin-deploy` tests, 2,792 safe Iris tests, 1,518 repository affected tests, mechanical lint/type checks, and the advisory branch review. No live controller or Pulumi stack was changed. Each new stack needs the documented one-time `pulumi stack init` before its first rollout.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 ### Research

`marin-deploy iris rollout` calls the controller provider's preflight before checkpointing or building images. The CoreWeave provider currently resolves only the controller signing key there; it first reads S3 credentials such as `CW_KEY_ID` and `CW_KEY_SECRET` during Kubernetes activation, after the expensive rollout preparation has completed.

### Proposed Fix

Validate the CoreWeave task environment during [`preflight_controller`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f8265d8a0c6dc6f558aab59bca617cc20f8a88c3/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/controller.py#L471-L474), including S3 credentials and `defaults.inject_env`. Missing variables will fail before the checkpoint and image build. Pulumi activation reads the same operator environment in its separate provider process, keeping secret values out of Pulumi inputs and state. PR #8652 already owns this deploy path; no other open PR overlaps the change.
